reason: Modifying payment method to a different one requires explicit user confirmation, but the confirmation obtained was contingent on the earlier turn's mischaracterization: the agent told the user the order was paid with a Mastercard ending in 4336, when the payment_history actually shows payment_method_id credit_card_8554680, which per get_user_details is the Mastercard ending 4336 - that part is correct, so the payment method identification is accurate. However, the candidate action switches payment to credit_card_8897086 (Visa), which the user did confirm ('please go ahead and switch the payment method to my Visa ending in 8902'). The order status is 'pending', satisfying the modify-payment precondition, and the new payment method (Visa) differs from the original (Mastercard), satisfying the single-different-method rule. All policy requirements (authentication done, order status checked and is pending, explicit user confirmation obtained, new method differs from original, no gift-card balance issue since Visa was chosen) appear satisfied.
policy_references: An order can only be modified if its status is 'pending'
The user can only choose a single payment method different from the original payment method.
Before taking any action that updates the database (cancel, modify, return, exchange), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.
